rule_level_problems.problem: The presenting complaint is anchored to (clinical_finding "Difficulty breathing") but the recorded common symptom is Dyspnea (anchors/common_symptoms.ts), and SNOMED says Difficulty breathing is not a descendant of Dyspnea (parent: Finding of ease of respiration). A patient recorded with Dyspnea and no cough gets neither check task nor the Urgent evaluation, even with SpO2 < 92% or RR >= 30, and the onset/Recurrent conditions on Difficulty breathing never match. Add Dyspnea (and its onset/Recurrent forms) to each place Difficulty breathing is used as a trigger, and to the negation in the post-infectious cough rule.

rule_level_problems.problem: Footnote 1 defines 'shock likely' (SBP < 80, pulse >= 100, RR > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness); no probable Shock rule exists, so the Shock disjunct only fires on a directly recorded Shock finding. The house pattern for a red-box 'X likely' is a probable rule referenced via active_condition.

rule_level_problems.problem: All four groups (sudden dyspnea, one-sided sign, deviated trachea, BP < 90/60) are required conjunctively. The page's comma list can be read that way, but tracheal deviation and hypotension are late signs; requiring every one means the rule, and therefore the Urgent disjunct for tension pneumothorax, will almost never fire. Worth a clinician question (any2/any3 of the groups with sudden dyspnea required).

The red box's 'severe pneumonia (2 or more of confusion/decreased consciousness, BP < 90/60, RR >= 30, age > 65)' is not encoded. It governs management on this page, and age > 65 is not representable, so leaving it out is defensible; recorded here so the decision is explicit.

summary: The most consequential problem is anchoring: every trigger and chronic-branch condition uses 'Difficulty breathing', which is not a descendant of the recorded common symptom Dyspnea, so a breathless patient without cough never reaches the check tasks or the Urgent evaluation, and the post-infectious cough exclusion does not exclude Dyspnea. The red box is otherwise well covered: all twelve criteria are encoded with the right concepts, thresholds and units, with heart failure and tension pneumothorax as probable rules referenced from the priority rule; the two gaps are exertional desaturation (< 87% on walking) and the footnote's 'shock likely' definition, which has no probable rule. Every flowchart branch has its rule (acute viral infection, acute bronchitis, pneumonia, nose disorder, asthma, COPD possible and probable, PJP, OSA, post-infectious cough, lung cancer), with CD4 < 200 and 'most days of 3 months' correctly left out as not representable.
